column3: Close to the Hebrew; “the distinguished of the first of the nations” is rendered “Notable persons in the chief nation.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV repeats “Woe to you” from verse 1, and renders “an evil day” “the day of doom.”
Close to the Hebrew; “who improvise to the sound of the lyre” is rendered “Who sing idly to the sound of stringed instruments.”
Close to the Hebrew; “they were not sickened” is rendered “are not grieved.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the revelry of the sprawlers will end” is rendered “those who recline at banquets shall be removed.”
Close to the Hebrew; “his loved one and the one who burns him” is rendered “a relative of the dead, with one who will burn the bodies,” and “hush!” “Hold your tongue!”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “there” in “Does one plow there with oxen?”, and renders “poison” “gall.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Lebo Hamath” is rendered “the entrance of Hamath,” and “the wadi of the Arabah” “the Valley of the Arabah.”
